parts.label: a
parts.technique: Systematic sampling
parts.reason: S1.1 explicitly lists systematic sampling as a technique students should be familiar with; describing selection of random start and every nth item is standard content.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Critique sampling technique
parts.reason: S1.1 requires ability to select or critique sampling techniques including disadvantages; this matches directly.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Probability within systematic sampling context
parts.reason: This part asks for the probability that a systematic sample includes both first and last item, which depends on understanding systematic sampling mechanics (sampling interval fixed by random start), a specific numeric/structural insight not stated in S1.1's guidance. However S1.1 covers systematic sampling as a technique and basic probability reasoning about it is a natural extension within that statement's scope; still, no statement mentions computing selection probabilities for systematic samples specifically, so it's borderline but plausibly covered by S1.1 as understanding of the technique.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient
parts.reason: Spearman's rank correlation is not mentioned anywhere in the S statements; S5.1 only covers PMCC (product moment correlation coefficient) hypothesis testing, and S2.2/S5.1 explicitly exclude calculation involving correlation coefficients via formula but do mention PMCC via calculator, not Spearman's. Spearman's rank is a named concept not covered.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hypothesis test using Spearman's rank correlation
parts.reason: Depends on Spearman's rank coefficient from part (a), which is out of spec; also no statement covers hypothesis testing with Spearman's rank (critical values table for rank correlation not mentioned).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Rationale for using rank correlation over PMCC
parts.reason: This explanation relies on understanding Spearman's rank vs PMCC, a topic not in spec.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Effect of tied ranks
parts.reason: Concept of tied ranks in Spearman's correlation, not covered by any statement.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Hypothesis test for mean using confidence interval
parts.reason: S5.3 covers hypothesis testing for the mean of a Normal distribution with known/given/assumed variance; using a CI to test a claim relates to this idea, though S5.3 doesn't explicitly cover using a given CI for testing. This is a natural extension within S5.3's scope.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Confidence interval for mean using sample variance (large sample z)
parts.reason: This is a standard CI construction for population mean, similar to logic underlying S5.3's z-test structure (X-bar ~ N(mu, sigma^2/n)), using z critical values; this matches methods implied by S5.3 even though CI construction itself isn't separately named, it's a natural companion calculation to the hypothesis test statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Binomial probability for number of CIs containing mu
parts.reason: Uses binomial distribution (S4.1) applied to a probability context involving confidence intervals; calculating binomial probabilities directly matches S4.1's coverage, though it requires understanding of CI coverage probability from (b)'s out-of-spec-adjacent context is actually fine since S4.1 covers binomial calc directly.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Chi-squared goodness of fit test
parts.reason: Chi-squared tests (goodness of fit) are not mentioned in any S statement; S2.4 explicitly says 'Significance tests, other than those mentioned in Section 5, will not be expected' and Section 5 only covers binomial proportion and normal mean tests, not chi-squared.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Expected frequency calculation for contingency table (chi-squared test of association)
parts.reason: Part of chi-squared test of association, not covered by any statement and excluded per S2.4.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Degrees of freedom for chi-squared test
parts.reason: Chi-squared test concept entirely absent from spec statements.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Two-sample z-test for difference of means
parts.reason: Hypothesis testing for difference between two population means is not covered; S5.3 only covers a test for the mean of a single Normal distribution, not two-sample tests. This is a distinct, unlisted technique.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Assumptions for two-sample test
parts.reason: Relies on the out-of-spec two-sample hypothesis test framework from (a).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Combining sample statistics / unbiased variance estimate with pooled data
parts.reason: This concerns combining sums to find unbiased variance estimator for an updated sample; while S2.3 covers standard deviation/variance calculation including from summary statistics, this specific technique of updating sums (Σx, Σx²) from combined data isn't fully matched, but S2.3 does state 'calculate standard deviation, including from summary statistics' which covers manipulating Sxx-type sums. It's a plausible extension.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sum of independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: Normal distribution linear combination (sum of independent normals) is not covered by S4.2, which only covers the single Normal distribution as a model and finding probabilities, not combinations/sums of normal variables (a distinct technique not stated anywhere in the S statements).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Difference of independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: Same issue as (a); linear combinations of normal distributions not in spec.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Linear combination of independent Normal random variables (G - 2T)
parts.reason: Same issue; combinations of normal random variables entirely absent from spec statements.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Central Limit Theorem applied to uniform distribution
parts.reason: Central Limit Theorem is explicitly excluded: S5.3 states 'Knowledge of the Central Limit Theorem or other large sample approximations is not required.' Also uniform distribution/continuous random variable mean-variance not covered.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Confidence interval using CLT result for uniform distribution parameter
parts.reason: Depends on the CLT-based distribution derived in (a), which is explicitly excluded per S5.3.
